dimensions.name: Strategy Coherence
dimensions.tagline: Is this actually a strategy, or a list of priorities?

skills.name: Kernel of Good Strategy
skills.tag: Diagnosis + guiding policy + coherent actions: Rumelt's three-part test for a real strategy

skills.name: Wardley Mapping
skills.tag: Map where each component sits on the evolution curve — is your claimed differentiation actually defensible?

skills.name: First Principles
skills.tag: Strip inherited assumptions — what does the business actually know vs. believe about its position?

skills.name: Red Teaming
skills.tag: Before the strategy is announced, mandate an independent team to find the conditions under which it fails

chain.name: Scenario Planning
chain.tag: Model multiple plausible futures before committing to one strategic path

questions: Can you state the strategy as a diagnosis plus guiding policy in one sentence?
What is the single assumption the strategy depends on — and when was it last stress-tested?
Which components of your competitive advantage are evolving toward commodity?
Has the strategy been challenged by someone with no stake in its success — or only by its authors?

dimensions.name: Portfolio Economics
dimensions.tagline: Does each unit earn its keep — and is the investment split intentional?

skills.name: Unit Economics
skills.tag: Does the model work per customer? LTV:CAC, payback period, contribution margin at the unit level

skills.name: Value Creation and Capture
skills.tag: Creating value and keeping some of it are two different problems — check both separately

skills.name: Three Horizons
skills.tag: Is investment actively spread across core, emerging, and future — or all piled into Horizon 1?

chain.name: Pricing Decision
chain.tag: Full chain: value created, cost floor, competitive ceiling, customer psychology

questions: Which business units are value creators vs. value consumers at the margin?
What is the investment split across the three horizons — and is it a deliberate choice?
Where is value being created for customers that the business is not capturing?

dimensions.name: Delivery & Throughput
dimensions.tagline: Is work flowing, or stalling at hidden chokepoints?

skills.name: Bottlenecks
skills.tag: The single constraint that governs throughput — improvements elsewhere don't move the system

skills.name: Cost of Delay
skills.tag: The economic cost of delivering one period later — makes the invisible cost of slowness visible

skills.name: WIP Limits
skills.tag: Explicit caps on in-progress work that pull rather than push — the primary lever for faster flow

chain.name: Improve Delivery Flow
chain.tag: Structured diagnostic: map the flow, find the constraint, reduce WIP, measure outcomes

questions: Can the team name the single constraint on throughput right now?
Where does work spend the most time waiting rather than being actively worked on?
What is the ratio of in-progress work to work completed in the last month?

dimensions.name: Innovation Pipeline
dimensions.tagline: Is the organisation experimenting at the right rate — and killing the right things?

skills.name: Innovation Health Indicators
skills.tag: Five dimensions of innovation readiness: portfolio balance, process discipline, people, culture, metrics

skills.name: From Idea to Hypothesis
skills.tag: Convert ideas into falsifiable predictions with explicit kill conditions before committing experiment resource

skills.name: Three Horizons
skills.tag: A healthy innovation portfolio has active bets in all three horizons, not just optimisation of the core

skills.name: A/B Testing
skills.tag: The operational instrument for hypothesis testing — pre-specified metric, calculated sample size, no peeking

chain.name: Innovation Capability Diagnostic
chain.tag: Structured readiness assessment across five innovation dimensions

questions: When did the organisation last kill an initiative based on evidence rather than politics or attachment?
What fraction of investment sits in Horizon 3 — and is that fraction a deliberate choice?
How many hypotheses are in active experiment right now, with explicit kill criteria defined in advance?
Are experiments designed to be capable of returning a negative result — or structured to confirm?

dimensions.name: Metric Integrity
dimensions.tagline: Are measures surfacing truth, or generating compliance theatre?

skills.name: Goodhart's Law
skills.tag: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure — audit every headline KPI

skills.name: Outcome vs Output
skills.tag: Activity metrics measure busyness; outcome metrics measure what the business actually needs

skills.name: Calibration
skills.tag: Are forecasts reliable? Track whether confidence levels match actual outcomes systematically

questions: Which KPIs are most likely being gamed — optimised for the measure rather than the goal it was meant to proxy?
How often do forecasts match outcomes, and are misses investigated or explained away?
Which metrics haven't moved in years despite stated priority — and what does that signal?
dimensions.overlap: Goodhart's Law also appears in Incentive Alignment (dimension 7). The same mechanism — optimising for the measure rather than the goal — drives both metric gaming and incentive distortion. Review both dimensions together.

dimensions.name: Culture & Change Readiness
dimensions.tagline: Can the organisation actually execute the changes it announces?

skills.name: Psychological Safety
skills.tag: Do people surface bad news early? Safety to speak up is the precondition for honest organisational information

skills.name: Immunity to Change
skills.tag: Hidden competing commitments explain why rational plans fail — this is structural, not personal resistance

skills.name: Organizational Culture
skills.tag: Culture is what the organisation rewards and tolerates, not what it states in values documents

chain.name: Transformation Chain
chain.tag: End-to-end sequence for designing and executing large-scale organisational change

questions: Does bad news arrive quickly and unpolished, or slowly and curated?
Which change initiatives have stalled — and what is the real, unstated reason?
Who are the informal opinion leaders — and are they inside or outside the change coalition?

dimensions.name: Incentive Alignment
dimensions.tagline: Do reward structures drive the behaviour the strategy actually needs?

skills.name: Incentives
skills.tag: Behaviour follows reward structures — check what is actually being incentivised, not what is intended

skills.name: Principal–Agent Problem
skills.tag: Where do BU leader incentives diverge from group goals? The gap reliably predicts the behaviour you see

skills.name: Goodhart's Law
skills.tag: Targets that become measures get optimised at the expense of the underlying goal

questions: What behaviours are incentive structures actually rewarding — and are those the behaviours the strategy needs?
Where do business unit leader incentives diverge most sharply from group-level goals?
Which targets are being consistently hit but feel hollow — and what does that signal?
dimensions.overlap: Goodhart's Law also appears in Metric Integrity (dimension 5). The same mechanism drives both metric gaming and incentive distortion. Review both dimensions together.

dimensions.name: Risk & Drift
dimensions.tagline: Are safety margins eroding in ways nobody is currently naming?

skills.name: Drift to Failure
skills.tag: Systems migrate toward unsafe boundaries through accumulated reasonable decisions — visible only in hindsight

skills.name: Margin of Safety
skills.tag: The buffer between current state and critical threshold — how much has been quietly eroded for efficiency?

skills.name: Second-Order Effects
skills.tag: What happens after what happens? Trace the downstream consequences of current decisions and trade-offs

skills.name: Steelmanning
skills.tag: Build the strongest possible case that the risk picture is worse than the organisation currently believes

questions: What has been normalised in the last two years that would have alarmed leadership when it first appeared?
Where are operational buffers being squeezed — and what failure does that historically precede?
What is the next thing that could go seriously wrong that nobody is currently discussing?
Can anyone in the room articulate the best case that the current risk posture is dangerously optimistic?

dimensions.name: AI Exposure
dimensions.tagline: Where is AI making decisions — and is governance keeping pace with deployment?

skills.name: AI Authority Boundaries
skills.tag: Six registers where AI may not be a decision-maker — map current deployments against each

skills.name: Minimal Capability Principle
skills.tag: Deploy the minimum capability needed for the task — excess capability creates excess and hard-to-audit risk

skills.name: Observer Bias
skills.tag: Evaluators who built the system are poorly placed to assess whether it works — structure in independence

chain.name: AI Use Case Autonomy Assessment
chain.tag: Pre-deployment chain: authority, reversibility, oversight design, and escalation paths

questions: Where is AI currently making — or materially influencing — decisions that humans used to make?
Which AI deployments have explicit reversal mechanisms if the system produces a bad outcome?
Where does the organisation have unmanaged AI exposure rather than governed AI capability?

dimensions.name: Operating Model Alignment
dimensions.tagline: Does the way the organisation is structured enable or impede the strategy?

skills.name: Conway's Law
skills.tag: Systems — organisational ones included — mirror the communication structures that built them

skills.name: Team Topologies
skills.tag: Four team types and three interaction modes: does your structure produce the flow the strategy requires?

skills.name: RACI Framework
skills.tag: One Accountable per decision — where accountability is unclear, both speed and quality suffer

chain.name: Org Design for Flow Diagnostic
chain.tag: Structured diagnostic: does the org design enable fast, independent delivery of strategic outcomes?

questions: Where does the organisational structure create the most friction for executing the stated strategy?
Which decisions slow down most — and is it unclear ownership or unnecessary cross-team dependency?
Does the team topology match the architecture and capabilities the strategy requires?
